column.name: nominator_name
column.value: Calvin Ho

column.name: nominee_name
column.value: Sarah Murphy

column.name: practice
column.value: Data & AI

column.name: what_text
column.value: Led the automation of the client onboarding pipeline, cutting a five-day manual process down to under four hours. She rebuilt the ingestion step, wrote the regression suite that now guards it, and personally shadowed the operations team for a fortnight so the handover stuck.

column.name: how_text
column.value: This demonstrated Innovation and Customer Success. Sarah wasn't asked to do this - she spotted the bottleneck in a retro, quantified the cost to the client, and built the business case herself before writing a line of code. The client has since cited the turnaround time in their renewal.

column.name: ai_rationale
column.value: Specific, quantified impact (five days to four hours) with a named beneficiary and evidence of initiative beyond the assigned role. The HOW names two core values and ties each to concrete behaviour rather than restating the WHAT.

column.name: nominator_name
column.value: Mark Dalton

column.name: nominee_name
column.value: Ravi Patel

column.name: practice
column.value: Cloud Engineering

column.name: what_text
column.value: Ran the Azure migration for the largest account in the region across a three-week cutover, including two unplanned rollbacks at 2am that he handled without escalating to the client.

column.name: how_text
column.value: Excellence, plainly. Ravi kept a calm, methodical approach through a genuinely difficult migration and made sure two junior engineers were paired with him for every rollback so the knowledge did not leave with him.

column.name: ai_rationale
column.value: Concrete scope and a clear account of behaviour under pressure. Slightly weaker on measurable outcome than the strongest nominations, but the knowledge-transfer detail evidences the value claimed.

column.name: how_text

column.name: how_text
column.value: Good job by James on the audit. Nice work all round and a real team player.

column.name: nominator_name
column.value: Sophie Martin

column.name: nominee_name
column.value: Conor Byrne

column.name: practice
column.value: Managed Services

column.name: what_text
column.value: Rebuilt the on-call runbook after a Sev-1 exposed that three of the documented recovery steps no longer worked. He then ran a game-day exercise so the whole rota had practised the new procedure before it was needed for real.

column.name: how_text
column.value: Integrity - Conor could have quietly patched the runbook and moved on. Instead he wrote an honest post-incident review naming what was wrong, circulated it to the account team, and made sure the fix was proven rather than assumed.

column.name: ai_rationale
column.value: Strong on behaviour and clearly ties Integrity to a specific choice the nominee made. Impact is described qualitatively rather than measured, which is the main thing holding the score below the top band.

column.name: nominator_name
column.value: Jamie Doyle

column.name: nominee_name
column.value: Alex Rivera

column.name: practice
column.value: Cloud Engineering

column.name: what_text
column.value: Alex led the release rollout over a tight weekend window and saved the client two full days of downtime. He coordinated four teams across two time zones and personally verified each of the eleven cutover steps before signing off.

column.name: how_text
column.value: Collaboration and Excellence. Rather than working the weekend alone, Alex built a rota so nobody did more than one night shift, then ran the bridge call himself so the client always had one point of contact. Nobody on the team burned out and the client saw a single calm voice throughout.

column.name: ai_rationale
column.value: A substantial improvement on the original submission. Quantified impact (two days of downtime avoided), specific scope (four teams, eleven steps), and the HOW names two values and evidences each with a distinct decision. No gaps remaining.

column.name: nominator_name
column.value: Priya Nair

column.name: nominee_name
column.value: Hannah Byrne

column.name: what_text
column.value: Took over a stalled discovery phase three weeks in, re-scoped it with the client in a single workshop, and delivered the findings pack on the original date despite the lost time.

column.name: how_text
column.value: Customer Success. Hannah put the client's deadline ahead of a comfortable re-plan, and was straight with them about what would and would not fit in the remaining time rather than promising everything.

column.name: nominator_name
column.value: John Walsh

column.name: nominee_name
column.value: Aisling Kelly

column.name: what_text
column.value: Rescued the public sector bid after the incumbent lead went on emergency leave nine days before submission. Aisling picked up a half-finished response, rewrote the three weakest sections, and the bid was shortlisted.

column.name: how_text
column.value: Excellence and Community. She pulled in help from four practices without a single escalation, and made a point of crediting the original author's work in the debrief rather than presenting the rescue as her own.

column.name: ai_rationale
column.value: Clear high-stakes context, a measurable outcome (shortlisted), and a HOW that evidences both values with specific choices. Among the strongest nominations in the current set.

column.name: nominee_name
column.value: Michael Chen

column.name: practice
column.value: Managed Services

column.name: what_text
column.value: Cut the monthly reporting run from eleven hours to forty minutes by replacing a chain of spreadsheets with a scheduled job, then trained two analysts to maintain it so it did not become his private tool.

column.name: how_text
column.value: Innovation. Michael was not asked for this - he tracked how long the manual run took for three months, presented the numbers, and only then proposed the change. The training step is what turned a clever script into something the team actually owns.

column.name: ai_rationale
column.value: Quantified before-and-after with evidence the nominee gathered the baseline themselves. The handover detail distinguishes this from a one-off automation.
